sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Count a defined action, in a defined context.

children: An
observable action
is something a person actually does. The
numerator
counts the defined outcome; the
denominator
counts eligible opportunities using the same unit.
Missing
means you lack a usable record, not that the action succeeded or failed.
Action versus intention
“I would use it” is a reported intention. Selecting the correct route in a prototype task is an observed action in that test. Neither automatically establishes actual adoption or payment.
Assistance matters
Record whether the facilitator coached or helped. Separate unassisted success from assisted completion, partial, failure, abandonment and unknown.
Bring the claim and format from Lesson 32.
Define action start/end and outcome categories before testing.
Choose a consistent counting unit and eligible denominator.
Plan anonymous records, context, assistance and source references.
Preserve duplicate, missing and excluded-record information.
Interpret only within the actual source, task and sample scope.
Fictional counting example — practice only

Five unique role-play participants are listed. Four have a known eligible task opportunity; one lacks a usable opportunity record and is separately marked unknown. Of the four known opportunities, two complete unassisted, one completes with help and one does not complete. Report “2 of 4 known eligible participants completed unassisted; 1 opportunity record unknown.” Explain how the unknown could affect the result. Do not claim half the market will adopt.

Multiple clicks or attempts by one person are not multiple unique participants. If attempts are your unit, label them as attempts. Predefine inclusion/exclusion and report missingness; do not drop awkward records to improve the result. A small convenience test does not estimate a market-wide conversion rate.

If no test ran, counts are “not run,” not measured zeros. Prepare a blank count template. Keep rehearsal values fictional. No tracking SDK, analytics, task recording or experiment is connected here; use anonymous planning notes only.
